claims.text: In 2021-2025, age-standardised cancer mortality in Satakunta wellbeing services county was 9.7% above the national level (ratio 1.097, 95% interval 1.063-1.132), about 58.7 more deaths a year than its age structure predicts.

Referrals for specialised health care received after processing for more than 21 days, % of the referrals received: Satakunta wellbeing services county is at 3 (three-year mean to 2025) against 1 nationally.
Among the stages that public data can measure, the earliest one where Satakunta wellbeing services county is clearly worse than the country is referral into specialist care.

Time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county for any cancer, so the Goal 3 indicator "patients access treatment within the established target times" cannot be checked from open data.

Recommended: standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral. Under the stated assumptions this postpones about 11.7 deaths a year in Satakunta wellbeing services county (range 1.7-23.5) for an assumed EUR 315,168 a year; it stayed in the portfolio in 95% of sensitivity runs.

Proportion of women invited to cervical cancer screening (smear test) who attended, %: 72.1% against the 80% target. HPV self-sampling kits for cervical screening non-attenders is expected to add 1.5-4.5 percentage points, closing about 38% of the gap.

Proportion of invited to colorectal cancer screening who attended, %: 74.4% against the 80% target. Reminder and multilingual re-invitation for colorectal screening is expected to add 1.5-4.5 percentage points, closing about 53% of the gap.
First step for every county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.
